facts.text: I have a painful open sore on my right leg.
It started as a small red spot.
It has gotten bigger since then.
The middle of it looks like dead tissue, and the edges are purplish and irregular.

facts.item: leg sore: insect bite at the site
facts.text: An ant bit me at that spot before the sore appeared.
My feet are swollen, and pressing on the swelling leaves a dent.
I have swollen, twisted veins in both of my lower legs.
I had anterior uveitis, an inflammation in my eye.
I was treated with corticosteroids for the uveitis 8 months ago.
I got back from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.
I don't have any other symptoms elsewhere in my body.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on the anterior right leg with a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders; tender to palpation.

findings.name: lower limb examination
findings.result: Pitting pedal edema; dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

findings.name: peripheral pulses
findings.result: Femoral and pedal pulses palpable bilaterally.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: WBC normal; hemoglobin normal; platelets normal.

findings.name: skin biopsy of the leg lesion
findings.result: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

f005: 'Central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders' is listed as a secondary symptom; kept because the patient can see her own lesion, worded in lay terms. The same description is in the skin exam (x004).
f007: 'Pitting' edema is worded as what the patient notices (pressing leaves a dent). The source says 'pedal edema of the lower extremities' without a side; the exam does not give one either.
f019: From the ROS line 'No additional systemic symptoms mentioned.', read as a negative review of systems (CONVERSION.md treats 'No ... provided' meta phrases as denials when they carry that meaning).

x004.source_text: A 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on the anterior right leg with a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders. Pitting pedal edema is noted along with dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. + Tenderness over the lesion. Femoral and pedal pulses palpable bilaterally.

x001: 37.6°C is 99.7°F, not 98°F; the source's two units disagree. Kept as written (see source_issues).
x004: The two skin-exam leaves are split by what a doctor requests: the lesion itself (x004), leg edema and veins (x005), and peripheral pulses (x006).

leakage.reason: The skin biopsy result names the diagnosis (pyoderma gangrenosum). This is the test's answer; the finding name does not reveal it.

source_issues: Temperature '37.6°C (98°F)': the Celsius and Fahrenheit values disagree (37.6°C = 99.7°F).
Diagnosis text is visible in Test_Results (pool flag visible_gold_alias_partitions = test_results): the skin biopsy names pyoderma gangrenosum.
notes: The ant bite (History and p003) is one context child of the leg sore. The lesion's appearance, its start as a small red spot, its growth and its 1-month duration are children of f001.

The past medical history appears in both History and Past_Medical_History; each condition is one fact citing both. The uveitis episode and its corticosteroid treatment 8 months ago are a medical-history fact and a past-medication fact.
The ROS line 'No additional systemic symptoms mentioned.' is kept as a denial of other symptoms (f019).

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on her leg.
